## Formal {.unnumbered}

$$
    W = \frac{(\sum_{i = 1}^n a_i x_{(i)})^2}{\sum_{i = 1}^n (x_i - \bar{x})^2}
$${#eq-shapiro}

## Examples {.unnumbered}

```{r}
#| echo: true
#| code-fold: false
#| fig-cap: "Shapiro-Wilk Test for Normality"
#| label: fig-shapiro-test

# Example 1: Test data from a normal distribution
set.seed(123)
normal_data <- rnorm(100, mean = 0, sd = 1)

# Run Shapiro-Wilk test
result1 <- shapiro.test(normal_data)
print("Test on normally distributed data:")
print(result1)

# Example 2: Test data from a non-normal distribution
non_normal_data <- rexp(100, rate = 1)

result2 <- shapiro.test(non_normal_data)
print("Test on exponentially distributed data:")
print(result2)

# Interpretation:
# If p-value > 0.05: we fail to reject the null hypothesis (data is normally distributed)
# If p-value < 0.05: we reject the null hypothesis (data is NOT normally distributed)
```

```{r}
#| echo: true
#| code-fold: false
#| fig-cap: "Q-Q Plots for Normality Assessment"
#| label: fig-qq-shapiro

# Set up 1x2 panel layout
par(mfrow = c(1, 2))

# Panel 1: Q-Q plot for normal data
qqnorm(normal_data, main = "Q-Q Plot: Normal Data")
qqline(normal_data, col = "red", lwd = 2)

# Panel 2: Q-Q plot for non-normal (exponential) data
qqnorm(non_normal_data, main = "Q-Q Plot: Exponential Data")
qqline(non_normal_data, col = "red", lwd = 2)

# Reset plot layout
par(mfrow = c(1, 1))
```
